title_en: Answers on the explanation of hadith 2
body_ar:
شرح الحديث: «كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا" نرجو منكم توضيحا لمعنى الحديث التالي: «كتب على ابن آدم حظه من الزنا وهو مدرك ذلك لا محالة فالعين تزني وزناها النظر والأذن تزني وزناها السمع والفرج يصدق ذلك أو يكذبه»؟

أن رسول الله (ص) بين أن الزنا من الأمور المنتشرة فهو مثل الشرك، فالشرك كثير الانتشار جدا وهو أخفى في النفوس من دبيب النمل، كما بين النبي (ص)، ولهذا قال الله تعالى: {وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون} ولهذا كان النبي (ص) يقول في دعائه: «اللهم إني أعوذ بك أن أشرك بك وأنا أعلم وأستغفرك لما لا أعلم»، مثل ذلك الزنا فهو أيضا أنواع منوعة، وهو منتشر خفي، فكثير من الناس لا يقترفون الجريمة نفسها جريمة الزنا ولكنهم يقتربون منها والله حرم الاقتراب من الزنا ولم يذكر الزنا بنفسه في قوله: {ولا تقربوا الزنا} فلم يقل ولا تزنوا، وإنما قال ولا تقربوا الزنا، فهذا يقتضي تحريم النظر وتحريم الكلام في الريبة وتحريم الاقتراب والدخول على النساء والخلوة والخلطة وغير ذلك فكل ذلك داخل فيما حرمه الله سبحانه وتعالى في قوله ولا تقربوا...
body_en:
Explanation of the hadith: "The son of Adam's portion of fornication is written for him." We ask you for a clarification of the meaning of the following hadith: "The son of Adam's portion of fornication is written for him, and he will attain that inevitably. The eye fornicates, and its fornication is the look; the ear fornicates, and its fornication is listening; and the private part confirms that or gives it the lie"?

The Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, made clear that fornication is among the widespread matters: it is like associating partners with God (shirk). Shirk is very widely spread indeed, and it is more hidden in men's souls than the creeping of ants, as the Prophet, upon whom be peace, made clear. That is why God Most High said: {And most of them do not believe in God without associating partners with Him} (Sūrat Yūsuf 12:106). And that is why the Prophet, upon whom be peace, used to say in his supplication: "O God, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know." Fornication is like that: it too is of various kinds, and it is widespread and hidden. Many people do not commit the crime itself, the crime of fornication, but they approach it — and God has forbidden the approaching of fornication, and did not mention fornication itself, in His words: {And do not approach fornication} (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:32). He did not say "do not fornicate"; rather He said "do not approach fornication". This entails the prohibition of the look, the prohibition of speech in which there is cause for suspicion, and the prohibition of drawing near, of entering upon women, of being alone with them, of mingling with them, and of other things besides — all of that falls within what God, glorified and exalted, forbade in His words "and do not approach"...

flags.arabic: تحريم الاقتراب والدخول على النساء والخلوة والخلطة
flags.context: the list of what the prohibition of 'approaching' is said to entail
options: the prohibition of drawing near, of entering upon women, of being alone with them, of mingling with them
the prohibition of approach, of visiting women, of seclusion and of free association
the prohibition of approaching and entering upon women, and of seclusion and mixing
flags.note: Khalwah is a man and a woman who may marry each other being alone together, a defined category in fiqh; khulṭah is unstructured mixing. Neither is 'seclusion' in its ordinary English sense, and option 1's 'seclusion' would be read by an English reader as the confinement of women, which is not what the word says. The pronoun 'with them' has been supplied in the English for both terms, since the Arabic nouns are absolute and English requires an object; the supply is marked here rather than made silently.

translator_notes: TYPING DECISION. The source presents this page as 'answers' (ajwibah) to questions put to the Sheikh, in the same question-and-answer form as the written fatwas. It is typed 'article' rather than 'fatwa' because it contains no ruling on an act: the glossary fixes fatwā as 'a considered legal opinion', and this page is explanatory. The site must not display it as a fatwa, or readers will take its contents for rulings.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'Fornication' renders zinā throughout. The term covers unlawful sexual intercourse whether or not either party is married; 'adultery' would be narrower than the Arabic.

The Sheikh's argument is an inference from the wording of the verse — that God prohibited approaching the act rather than the act itself — and the inference is preserved as a step rather than collapsed into its conclusion.
The hadith is given without a named collection and without a grading; none has been supplied. The supplication against unknowing shirk is likewise given without attribution.
The verse references have been supplied per house style; the source gives the verse texts alone.
The three dots at the end are in the source.
